First Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Introduction

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: This Act establishes the CSA Public Companies Authority and sets out the legal framework under which companies serve as public beneficiary companies of the Continental Security Agency.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: This Act shall be cited as the "Public Bonds Companies Act."

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The main purposes of this Act are:

items.text: to establish the CSA Public Companies Authority as the regulatory body of the CSA for Public Bonds Companies;
to provide for the placement of companies under the jurisdiction of the CSA, and for the shareholding of the CSA in those companies;
to set out the structure and governance of the Boards of Public Bonds Companies;
to govern the finance, funding, oversight and reporting of Public Bonds Companies;
to set out the requirements for compliance and the measures taken for breaches;
to provide for the withdrawal and dissolution of Public Bonds Companies; and
to ensure that Public Bonds Companies are governed transparently and accountably, and operate for the public benefit of the CSA.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: This Act applies to:

items.text: the CSA Public Companies Authority and the PCA Board;
every Public Bonds Company;
every subcompany, agency, body and institution under a Public Bonds Company; and
every director, officer, member of personnel, shareholder and member of the companies and bodies mentioned in this Article’s (a) (2) and (3)

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: This Act applies to a Public Bonds Company wherever it is incorporated or operates.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: This Act does not apply to a company that has not been placed under the Authority, except for private educational institutions receiving funding under Article 53 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: This Act shall be read together with the Constitution of the Continental Security Agency and with the laws, regulations and guidelines of the Continental Security Agency.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company incorporated under the laws of any state or nation remains subject to those laws. This Act applies in addition to them.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Where the Articles of Association, Memorandum of Association or bylaws of a Public Bonds Company are inconsistent with this Act, this Act prevails, and the inconsistent provision has no effect to the extent of the inconsistency.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Where an earlier instrument of the Continental Security Agency is inconsistent with this Act on a matter within its scope, this Act prevails.

blocks.text: Second Chapter
blocks.subtitle: The Public Companies Authority

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The CSA Public Companies Authority (PCA) is hereby established.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Authority sits under the Department of Economy and Trade, with the same rank as the other departments of the Department of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Cabinet vests in the Authority jurisdiction, legal powers and executive powers over all Public Bonds Companies, and over the subcompanies, agencies, bodies and institutions under them.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Authority is the regulatory body of the CSA for Public Bonds Companies.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The seat of the Authority is in New York City, New York.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The PCA Board may hold its meetings at any place within the jurisdiction of the CSA.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority shall:

items.text: regulate, monitor and evaluate Public Bonds Companies;
keep the Register of Public Bonds Companies, and register the seals of Public Bonds Companies and the businesses registered under them;
issue, renew and suspend Public Bonds Company Licences and Business Licences under the Sixth Chapter of this Act;
issue profile sheets under Article 24 of this Act;
ensure that Public Bonds Companies comply with this Act, the Constitution of the CSA, and the laws, regulations and guidelines of the CSA;
issue the Corporate Governance Code, the Board Code of Conduct and PCA Policies;
receive, review and act on the reports of Public Bonds Companies;
appoint Company Secretaries under Article 43 of this Act;
receive the submissions of Public Bonds Companies and pass them on under Article 19 of this Act;
advise the Director on the appointment and removal of Boards, and on the placement, withdrawal and dissolution of companies;
take measures for breaches under the Eleventh Chapter of this Act; and
report to the Department of Economy and Trade, the Cabinet and the Continental Assembly under the Tenth Chapter of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: In carrying out its functions, the Authority may:

items.text: request any information, record or document from a Public Bonds Company;
inspect the premises, records and accounts of a Public Bonds Company;
issue directions to a Public Bonds Company to comply with this Act;
approve or refuse borrowing under Article 55 of this Act;
suspend licences under Article 30 of this Act;
take measures under Article 61 of this Act; and
do anything else necessary to carry out its functions under this Act.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The powers of the Authority are exercised by the PCA Board, or by the President or the Secretary General where the PCA Board so delegates.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority has the following industries:

items.text: Aviation & Airport Operation;
Banking and Finance;
Business Development;
Courier Service;
Education;
General Trading;
Hajj Operation;
Marketing and Media;
National Health Insurance;
Pharmaceutical & Medical Supplies;
Ports Operation;
Real Estate & Urban Development;
Telecommunication;
Tourism;
Transport and Contracting; and
Utility.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Each Public Bonds Company falls under one or more industries, as stated in its mandate and recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Director may add or remove industries by an instrument published in the CSA Gazette.

blocks.text: Third Chapter
blocks.subtitle: The PCA Board

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority is led by the PCA Board.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The PCA Board is composed of seven members: the President, the Vice President and five Members.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Each of the five Members shall hold the title “Member of the PCA Board.”

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The President, the Vice President and the five Members are appointed by the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Continental Assembly may appeal the appointment of the President. The procedure for an appeal is governed by the rules of the Continental Assembly.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Appointments to the PCA Board are published in the CSA Gazette.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Members of the PCA Board hold office without a fixed term, until reappointment by the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A member of the PCA Board may resign by written notice to the Director.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Where a position on the PCA Board becomes vacant, the Director shall appoint a person to fill it.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Where the office of President is vacant, the Vice President acts as President until an appointment is made.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A person appointed to the PCA Board shall have knowledge or experience in business, finance, economics, law or public administration.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A person may not be a member of the PCA Board while serving on the Board of a Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A person may not be a member of the PCA Board while holding shares in a Public Bonds Company, unless the holding has been declared to and approved by the Director.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A person found by the Authority to have committed a breach under Article 60 of this Act may not be appointed to the PCA Board for the period set by PCA Policies.

blocks.title: Duties of the President and the Vice President

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The President leads the Authority and chairs the meetings of the PCA Board.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The President represents the Authority before the DET, the Cabinet, the Continental Assembly and other bodies.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The President is responsible for the quarterly reports of the Authority under Article 57 of this Act.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Vice President assists the President, and acts as President when the President is absent or unable to act, or when the office of President is vacant.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The PCA Board shall meet at least once each quarter.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The quorum for a meeting of the PCA Board is five members.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Decisions of the PCA Board are made by a simple majority of the members present and voting.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Where the votes are equal, the person chairing the meeting has a casting vote.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: Other procedures of the PCA Board are governed by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A member of the PCA Board who has a personal, financial or family interest in a matter before the PCA Board shall declare that interest before the matter is considered.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The member shall not take part in the discussion of, or vote on, that matter.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A member who fails to declare an interest may be removed by the Director.

blocks.text: Fourth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Administration of the Authority

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority has a Secretary General, who heads the Secretariat of the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Secretary General is appointed by the President and is not a member of the PCA Board.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Secretary General manages the daily administration of the Authority, keeps the Register, issues profile sheets, signs Public Bonds Company Licences and Business Licences, keeps the records and minutes of the PCA Board, and carries out the decisions of the PCA Board.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Secretary General attends the meetings of the PCA Board without a vote.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority may employ the staff necessary to carry out its functions.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Staff of the Authority work Continental Security Service and fall under the jurisdiction of the CSA Human Resources Commission.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Staff of the Authority shall keep confidential any information obtained in the course of their work, except where disclosure is required by law. The disclosure of confidential information will be governed by the Department of Internal Affairs and the Department of Justice.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Submissions by a Public Bonds Company to the Director under this Act shall follow the chain of command: from the Public Bonds Company to the Authority, from the Authority to the DET, and from the DET to the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The DET may refer a submission to the Cabinet before it reaches the Director. The involvement of the Cabinet is not required.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The decision of the Director on a submission is returned to the Public Bonds Company through the same chain of command.

blocks.text: Fifth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Public Bonds Companies

blocks.title: Status as subsidiaries of the CSA

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company acts as a subsidiary of the CSA.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company is a public beneficiary company of the CSA and shall operate for public benefit.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company is under the jurisdiction, legal powers and executive powers of the Authority.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company remains a separate legal person and is responsible for its own debts and obligations.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall carry the suffix “CPbc.” in its name.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Every subcompany of a Public Bonds Company shall carry the suffix “CPbc.” in its name.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Associated bodies, including businesses registered under a Public Bonds Company, do not carry the suffix “CPbc.”

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company may keep any suffix required by the law under which it is incorporated, placed after “CPbc.”, such as “CPbc. LLC” or “CPbc. Ltd.”.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: A company that is not a Public Bonds Company may not use the suffix “CPbc.” or present itself as a Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: A company ceases to use the suffix on withdrawal or dissolution under the Twelfth Chapter of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A company is placed under the Authority by a mandate signed by the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A mandate shall state:

items.text: the name of the company and its new name with the suffix “CPbc.”;
the law under which the company is incorporated;
its industry or industries and its Sector Department;
its member companies, subcompanies and associated bodies, if any;
the shareholding of the CSA;
whether the company may have a Chairperson under Article 38 of this Act;
whether the company may appoint its own Board under Article 46 of this Act; and
the date on which the placement takes effect.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A mandate is published in the CSA Gazette.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: On placement, the independence of the company is overridden, and the company and all its directors, personnel and members fall under the jurisdiction of the Authority.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: A company placed under the Authority shall obtain a Public Bonds Company Licence under Article 28 of this Act.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: A sample mandate is set out in Appendix 1 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority shall keep a Register of Public Bonds Companies.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Register shall record, for each Public Bonds Company, the details set out in Appendix 2 of this Act, including its licence, its registered seal, its subcompanies, its associated bodies and the businesses registered under it.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Businesses registered under a Public Bonds Company shall be recorded separately from its subcompanies, so that each is clearly identified as a business and not as a Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall notify the Authority of any change to its registered details within the period set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: The Register is kept by the Secretary General.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: At the request of a Public Bonds Company, the Secretary General shall issue a profile sheet setting out the details recorded for the company in the Register.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company may submit its profile sheet to institutions, nationally or internationally, to validate its presence as a company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A profile sheet shows the details recorded in the Register on the date on which it is issued.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A sample profile sheet is set out in Appendix 4 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall register its company seal with the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The registered seal is recorded in the Register and shown on the profile sheet of the company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Where this Act requires a document to be submitted under the seal of a Public Bonds Company, the document shall bear its registered seal.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Each Public Bonds Company falls under the sector of the Department of the CSA responsible for its industry, as stated in its mandate.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Sector Department sets policy for the sector in which the company operates. The jurisdiction of the Authority over the company is not affected.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: For example, an educational Public Bonds Company falls under the Department of Education, and a medical or pharmaceutical Public Bonds Company falls under the Department of Health and Welfare.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every subcompany and associated body of a Public Bonds Company falls under the jurisdiction of the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A member company of a group of companies placed under the Authority, and every subcompany of a Public Bonds Company, is itself a Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A business registered under a Public Bonds Company is an associated body. It is not a company and is not a Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A business is registered under a Public Bonds Company by a Business Licence under Article 33 of this Act.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall notify the Authority before it establishes or acquires a subcompany or associated body.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: This Act applies to subcompanies and associated bodies in the same way as it applies to Public Bonds Companies, unless this Act states otherwise.

blocks.text: Sixth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Licensing

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall hold a Public Bonds Company Licence.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Licensing is handled by the Authority. A licence is issued by the Authority and signed by the Secretary of Economy and Trade and the Secretary General.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: In this Chapter, a reference to the Secretary of Economy and Trade includes any person acting in that position or holding it on an interim basis.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: An application for a licence is made to the Authority under the registered seal of the company.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company may not operate without a valid licence.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: The licence number, its term and its status are recorded in the Register and shown on the profile sheet of the company.

blocks.title: Term and renewal of a licence

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company Licence follows the administrative terms of the CSA, and expires at the end of the administrative term in which it is issued.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall renew its licence for the next administrative term, within the period set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A renewed licence is valid for the whole of the next administrative term.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company Licence may be suspended by the Authority or by the Secretary of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: When the licence of a company is suspended, its Board is suspended. When the Board of a company is suspended, its licence is suspended.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: During the suspension, the company works under the PCA Board.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The PCA Board may appoint a board, on its behalf, to manage the suspended company and to act as its Board during the suspension.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: The suspension ends when it is lifted by the Authority or by the Secretary of Economy and Trade, whichever suspended the licence.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: Suspensions are recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company Licence may be revoked only by the Secretary of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Authority may recommend the revocation of a licence to the Secretary of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A company whose licence is revoked may not operate as a Public Bonds Company. The Director shall then declare its withdrawal or dissolution under the Twelfth Chapter of this Act.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Revocations are recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Where the licence of a company is suspended or revoked, the Authority, the DET or the Director may, at their discretion, bar any member of the Board of that company from being registered or acting as a board member of another company.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The period of a bar is set by the body that imposes it.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Bars are recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A business may be registered under a Public Bonds Company only with a Business Licence.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Business Licence is issued by the Authority and signed by the Secretary General only.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A Business Licence is valid for a fixed term of five years from the date on which it is issued, and may be renewed.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Business Licence may be suspended by the Authority or by the Secretary of Economy and Trade, and may be revoked only by the Secretary of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: A business does not carry the suffix “CPbc.” and is recorded in the Register under the Public Bonds Company under which it is registered.

blocks.text: Seventh Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Shareholding

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The CSA holds 50% of the shares of every Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The CSA is the principal shareholder of every Public Bonds Company. Where another shareholder holds an equal number of shares, the CSA is treated as the principal shareholder.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The rights attached to the shares of the CSA are exercised by the Shares Representative under Article 39 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The distribution of the remaining 50% of the shares of a Public Bonds Company is at the discretion of the company.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall record the holders of its remaining shares and notify the Authority of them, and of any change, for entry in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The shares of the CSA in a Public Bonds Company may not be sold, transferred, pledged or otherwise disposed of without the written approval of the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Any transfer of the shares of the CSA is recorded in the Register.

blocks.text: Eighth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Boards of Public Bonds Companies

blocks.title: Composition and order of the Board

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Board of every Public Bonds Company is composed of, in the following order:

items.text: the Chairperson or Founder, where approved under Article 38 of this Act;
the Managing Director;
the Deputy Managing Director;
the Chief Executive Officer;
the Board Directors; and
the Company Secretary.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: There is no minimum or maximum number of Board Directors that may be appointed.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Every member of the Board may vote on matters before the Board.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Where no Chairperson is approved, the Managing Director is the highest position in the organizational structure of the company.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: Where a Board is appointed by the company under Article 46 of this Act, the titles and positions approved by the Director apply in place of those in (a) of this Article.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company may have a Chairperson only with the explicit approval of the Director, given in its mandate or in a separate written instrument.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Chairperson is the founder of the company. The position may be titled "Chairperson" or "Founder".

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Where approved, the Chairperson is the highest position in the organizational structure of the company.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Chairperson is not required to attend meetings of the Board. When attending, the Chairperson may vote.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: Where the Chairperson is absent, or where there is no Chairperson, the Managing Director chairs meetings of the Board.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The CSA, as principal shareholder, is in law the Managing Director of every Public Bonds Company.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Director shall appoint a person to the Board as Managing Director, to represent the CSA and its shares. In this capacity, the Managing Director is the Shares Representative.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Managing Director is a non-executive member of the Board.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: When acting for the shares of the CSA, the Shares Representative may, at their discretion, cast the vote attached to those shares and veto a resolution of the Board or of the shareholders.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: The Shares Representative exercises the rights of the CSA as shareholder at general meetings of the company, and acts on the directions of the Director in matters concerning the shares of the CSA.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Director shall appoint a Deputy Managing Director to the Board of every Public Bonds Company, except where the Deputy Managing Director is appointed under Article 46 of this Act.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Deputy Managing Director assists the Managing Director, and acts as Managing Director when the Managing Director is absent or unable to act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Deputy Managing Director is a non-executive member of the Board.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company has a Chief Executive Officer, who runs the company.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Chief Executive Officer is the only officer of the company and is responsible for its day-to-day management.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Chief Executive Officer is an executive member of the Board and is accountable to the Board.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Chief Executive Officer carries out the decisions of the Board and reports to it on the performance and operations of the company.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Board Director may hold a specialization corresponding to an officer function, such as finance, operations, technology, legal affairs or human resources, and is titled accordingly, such as "Director of Finance", “Director, Finance” or any other interpretations.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Board Directors with a specialization take the place of officers other than the Chief Executive Officer, such as a chief financial officer or a chief operating officer.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A Board Director with a specialization is an executive member of the Board and reports to the Chief Executive Officer on matters within that specialization.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Board Director without a specialization is a non-executive member of the Board.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company has a Company Secretary, appointed:

items.text: by the Director; or
by the Authority, with the signed approval of the Director.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Company Secretary is always appointed under (a) of this Article, including where the Board is appointed by the company under Article 46 of this Act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Company Secretary is the representative of the CSA on the Board, and is a separate position from the Shares Representative.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Company Secretary shall:

items.text: ensure that the company, and every subcompany and associated body under it, follows the Constitution of the CSA and keeps up with the laws, regulations and guidelines of the CSA;
ensure that the company complies with this Act, the Corporate Governance Code, the Board Code of Conduct and PCA Policies;
prepare the annual report of the company and submit it to the Authority under Article 58 of this Act;
keep the minutes of meetings of the Board and the statutory records of the company; and
report to the Authority any breach of which they become aware.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: The Company Secretary is a non-executive member of the Board.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The executive members of the Board are the Chief Executive Officer and the Board Directors with a specialization.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The non-executive members of the Board are the Chairperson, the Managing Director, the Deputy Managing Director, the Company Secretary and the Board Directors without a specialization.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A non-executive member does not take part in the day-to-day management of the company, but has the same right to vote as an executive member.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Members of the Board of a Public Bonds Company, and of the boards and governing bodies of its subcompanies and associated bodies, are appointed by the Director, except for:

items.text: the Chairperson, who holds office with the approval of the Director under Article 38 of this Act;
the Company Secretary, who is appointed under Article 43 of this Act; and
members appointed by the company under Article 46 of this Act.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Members of the Board hold office without a fixed term, until reappointment by the Director.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A member of the Board may resign by written notice to the Director, with a copy to the Authority.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Appointments, resignations and removals are recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: At the discretion of the Director, a Public Bonds Company may appoint its own Board.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Where the Director allows this, the Director shall appoint the Chairperson, where there is one, and the Managing Director.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Director may give the Managing Director the discretion to appoint the rest of the Board, including the Deputy Managing Director, the Chief Executive Officer and the Board Directors.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The company may set titles and positions for its Board that differ from those in Article 37 (a) of this Act.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: Where a Board is appointed, changed or made different under this Article, its titles, positions and members must be approved by the Director. To obtain approval, the company shall submit:

items.text: a written document under the registered seal of the company;
the composition of the Board; and
information on each member, such as a curriculum vitae.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: The submission under (e) of this Article is made through the chain of command under Article 19 of this Act.

clauses.label: (g)
clauses.text: The Company Secretary is appointed under Article 43 of this Act and not under this Article.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: When a company is placed under the Authority, its current directors remain in office until a new Board is appointed under this Chapter.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: During this period, the directors shall prepare the company for transition, including the handover of its records, accounts and assets to the new board.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: During this period, the current directors shall not take decisions outside the ordinary course of business without the approval of the Authority.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Board shall:

items.text: act in good faith in the interests of the company and the public benefit of the CSA;
set the strategy of the company and approve its annual plan and budget;
oversee the Chief Executive Officer and its management of the company;
ensure that the company keeps proper accounts and that its financial statements are audited under Article 54 of this Act;
ensure compliance with this Act, the Corporate Governance Code, the Board Code of Conduct and PCA Policies; and
cooperate with the Authority and provide information it requests.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Article 16 of this Act applies to members of a Board in the same way as it applies to members of the PCA Board, with the declaration made to the Board and recorded by the Company Secretary.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall have Articles of Association, a Memorandum of Association or bylaws.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The quorum, voting, meetings and other procedures of the Board are determined by the Articles of Association, the Memorandum of Association or the bylaws of the company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: These documents shall be consistent with this Act and shall be lodged with the Authority. Any amendment shall be lodged with the Authority within the period set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority shall issue a Corporate Governance Code for Public Bonds Companies and a Board Code of Conduct for members of Boards.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company and every member of its Board shall comply with these codes.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A failure to comply with these codes is a breach under Article 60 of this Act.

blocks.text: Ninth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Finance and Funding

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The CSA’s share of the profits of every Public Bonds Company is paid to the Department of Economy and Trade.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The remainder of the profit is distributed in accordance with the Articles of Association, the Memorandum of Association or the bylaws of the company.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Payments under (a) of this Article shall be made within the period set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: Receipts, invoice, bill or any other record of payment made to the Department of Economy and Trade must be also shared with the PCA.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Details of the funding of Public Bonds Companies are confidential and not subject to disclosure.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (a) of this Article does not prevent disclosure to the Director, the Cabinet, the DET or the Authority, or to the Continental Assembly in its oversight of the Authority.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The CSA Department of Education shall fund educational institutions as follows:

items.text: Private educational institution shall receive 30% funding by the Department of Education; and
Public educational institutions under the Public Companies Authority shall receive up to 100% funding by the Department of Education.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Funding under (a) of this Article may be applied to any expenditure of the institution.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Department of Education determines the amount of funding for each public educational institution, within the limit in (a) of this Article.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall keep proper accounts and prepare annual financial statements for each financial year.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The annual financial statements shall be audited by an auditor approved by the Authority.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The audited financial statements shall be submitted to the Authority with the annual report under Article 58 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall obtain the prior written approval of the Authority before borrowing any amount above the limit set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Authority shall consult the DET before approving borrowing under (a) of this Article.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company may not pledge or charge the shares of the CSA as security for any borrowing.

blocks.text: Tenth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Oversight and Reporting

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority is accountable to the Department of Economy and Trade, the Cabinet and the Continental Assembly.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The President, or a member of the PCA Board authorized by the President, shall appear before the Continental Assembly when summoned.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority shall report quarterly, four times a year, to the DET, the Cabinet and the Continental Assembly.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Each quarterly report shall cover the matters set out in Appendix 3 of this Act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Details of funding shall be reported in a confidential annex, in accordance with Article 52 of this Act.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Every Public Bonds Company shall submit an annual report to the Authority, prepared by its Company Secretary, to keep the company accountable to the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The annual report shall include:

items.text: the audited financial statements of the company;
the performance and activities of the company, its subcompanies, its associated bodies and the businesses registered under it;
any changes to its Board, shareholding, licence and registered seal; and
a statement of its compliance with this Act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The annual report shall be submitted within the period set by the PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company shall submit any other report or information the Authority requests.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority may at any time request information, records or documents from a Public Bonds Company, and may inspect its premises, records and accounts.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company, and the members of its Board and its personnel, shall cooperate with the Authority and provide what it requests within the period it sets.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A failure to cooperate is a breach under Article 60 of this Act.

blocks.text: Eleventh Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Compliance and Penalties

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A breach is any failure by a Public Bonds Company, a member of its Board or its personnel to comply with:

items.text: this Act;
the mandate placing the company under the Authority;
the Corporate Governance Code or the Board Code of Conduct;
PCA Policies; or
a direction of the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: Operating without a valid Public Bonds Company Licence or Business Licence is a breach.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Where a breach is found, the Authority may:

items.text: issue a written warning;
suspend the Chief Executive Officer of the company;
suspend the licence and the Board of the company under Article 30 of this Act;
recommend the revocation of the licence to the Secretary of Economy and Trade under Article 31 of this Act;
bar members of the Board under Article 32 of this Act; or
impose a fine, in an amount set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Authority may take more than one measure for the same breach.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Measures are recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority may recommend to the Director the removal of a Board, or of any member of a Board.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Director decides on the recommendation and, where a Board or a member is removed, appoints a replacement.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Before taking a measure other than a written warning, the Authority shall notify the company or person concerned of the breach and give them an opportunity to respond within the period set by PCA Policies.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The Authority shall record its decision and the reasons for it, and notify the company or person concerned.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: A company or person may ask the Director to review a measure. The decision of the Director is final.

blocks.text: Twelfth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Withdrawal and Dissolution

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A Public Bonds Company remains a subsidiary of the CSA until the Director declares its dissolution or its withdrawal from the Authority.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A declaration is signed by the Director and published in the CSA Gazette.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: On withdrawal, the company ceases to be a Public Bonds Company and to be under the jurisdiction of the Authority, from the date stated in the declaration.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The company shall remove the suffix “CPbc.” from its name.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The declaration shall state how the shares of the CSA in the company are dealt with.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The company shall pay to the DET any share of profits owed to the CSA up to the date of withdrawal.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text: The Public Bonds Company Licence of the company ceases to have effect.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text: The withdrawal is recorded in the Register.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: On dissolution, the company is wound up under the law under which it is incorporated.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: After its debts and liabilities are paid, the remaining assets of the company are distributed among its shareholders according to their shareholding. The portion of the CSA is paid to the DET.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: The Public Bonds Company Licence of the company, and the Business Licences of the businesses registered under it, cease to have effect.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: The Authority oversees the dissolution and records it in the Register.

blocks.text: Thirteenth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Transitional Provisions

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The Authority becomes functional only once the PCA Board is appointed under the Third Chapter of this Act.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The functions and powers of the Authority are not exercised until the PCA Board is appointed as per (a) of this Article by any other body.

blocks.title: Companies placed before the PCA Board is appointed

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: A mandate signed by the Director before the PCA Board is appointed is valid, and the company placed by it is a Public Bonds Company from the date stated in the mandate.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The functions of the Authority over that company begin when the PCA Board is appointed.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Until a new Board is appointed, the current directors of that company remain in office under Article 47 of this Act.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A company under this Article shall obtain a Public Bonds Company Licence within the period set by PCA Policies after the PCA Board is appointed.

blocks.text: Fourteenth Chapter
blocks.subtitle: Miscellaneous

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: The PCA Board shall issue PCA Policies governing its procedures and the matters within its functions, including the Register, licensing and renewal, reporting formats and deadlines, fines, accounts and audit, borrowing limits and the procedure for measures.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: PCA Policies shall be consistent with this Act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: PCA Policies are issued separately and are not published with this Act.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: PCA Policies bind every Public Bonds Company from the date on which they are issued to it.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: This Act comes into force on the date of its publication in the CSA Gazette.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: The functions of the Authority commence in accordance with Article 67 of this Act.
The Appendices of this Act form part of this Act and shall be read together with it.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: Words in the singular include the plural, and words in the plural include the singular.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: A reference to an Article, a Chapter or an Appendix is a reference to an Article, a Chapter or an Appendix of this Act.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the interpretation of this Act.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: A reference to a position by its title includes any person lawfully acting in that position.

clauses.label: (c)

title: Establishment of the Continental Security Agency Gazette

blocks.text: Director’s Order Number 01/2026
Establishment of the Continental Security Agency Gazette
Director’s Order
I, Enzo Hernandez, Director of the Continental Security Agency, state the following.
Whereas:

items.text: every body of the Continental Security Agency, including the Executive, the Continental Assembly, the Judiciary and the independent commissions, issues documents that must be made known to the bodies and persons to which they apply;

the Continental Security Agency has no single official publication in which those documents are published, and no common rules on how they are classified, created, numbered, cited, presented and published; and
the documents of the Continental Security Agency are published in English and in Dhivehi, and must carry the same meaning in both languages;

blocks.text: Under the authority vested in the Director to direct the affairs of the Continental Security Agency,

I, Enzo Hernandez, Director of the Continental Security Agency, hereby establish the CSA Gazette by this Order, and order that the documents of the Continental Security Agency shall be classified, created, numbered, cited, presented and published as follows:

items.text: The CSA Gazette is the official publication of the Continental Security Agency. The CSA Gazette shall be published by The Director's Office on www.gazette.csa, and every document published in it shall be available to the public from the date of its publication.

Every body of the CSA shall publish its Acts, Regulations, Guidelines and Notices only in the CSA Gazette, in accordance with this Order. A body of the CSA includes every department, office, division, authority, committee and other body of the Executive, the Continental Assembly, the Judiciary and every independent commission of the CSA.

The text of a document as published in the CSA Gazette is the official text of that document, and shall prevail over any other copy. An Act, Director's Order, Regulation or Guideline shall have no effect unless it is published in the CSA Gazette.
The Gazette Office is hereby established as a Section of the Public Relations Division of The Director's Office. The Gazette Office shall be run by the Public Relations Executive.
The functions of the Gazette Office are:

items.label: (a)
items.text: to receive the documents submitted for publication in the CSA Gazette;

items.label: (b)
items.text: to review every document submitted to it for compliance with this Order;

items.label: (c)
items.text: to return to the issuing body any document that does not comply with this Order, stating each matter that does not comply;

items.label: (d)
items.text: to assign document numbers in accordance with point 18 of this Order;

items.label: (e)
items.text: to publish documents in the CSA Gazette;

items.label: (f)
items.text: to maintain the Gazette Register in accordance with point 34 of this Order; and

items.label: (g)
items.text: to keep a permanent record of every document published in the CSA Gazette, including every document that has been amended or repealed.
Every document published in the CSA Gazette shall be one of the following types:

items.label: (a)
items.text: Act (ޤާނޫނު);

items.label: (b)
items.text: Director's Order (އަމުރު);

items.label: (c)
items.text: Regulation (ގަވާއިދު);

items.label: (d)
items.text: Guideline (އުޞޫލު); and

items.label: (e)
items.text: Notice (އިޢުލާން).

items.after: No document shall be published in the CSA Gazette as any other type. An amendment is not a separate type of document, and is a document of the same type as the document it amends. A Guideline may be titled either a Guideline or a Policy, and a document titled a Policy is a Guideline for every purpose of this Order.

items.text: An Act is the primary law of the CSA. An Act sets out the law on a subject, establishes bodies and confers powers and duties. An Act may be issued:

items.label: (a)
items.text: by any department of the CSA, after the Act has been ratified by the Continental Assembly; or

items.label: (b)
items.text: until the Continental Assembly establishes the ratification of Acts, by the Cabinet, by the Director, or by the Cabinet and the Director jointly.

items.after: An Act issued under (b) of this point shall have the same effect as an Act issued under (a) of this point.

items.text: A Director's Order is an order of the Director, issued to establish, structure or direct the bodies and affairs of the CSA within the authority of the Director. A Director's Order shall be issued only by the Director, and shall be binding on every body and person of the CSA to which it applies. Any reference in a document of the CSA to an "Executive Mandate" shall be read as a reference to a Director's Order.

A Regulation sets out the detailed rules required to carry out an Act or a Director's Order. A Regulation shall be made only under an enabling provision of an Act or a Director's Order, and only by the body named in that enabling provision. A Regulation shall be binding on every body and person to which it applies.
A Guideline sets out the procedures, standards, principles or policy that a body shall follow in carrying out its functions. A Guideline may be issued:

items.label: (a)
items.text: by the body named in an enabling provision of an Act, a Director's Order or a Regulation; or

items.label: (b)
items.text: by any body of the CSA, on matters within that body's own functions.

items.after: A Guideline issued under (b) of this point shall apply only within the functions of the body that issued it.

items.text: A Notice is an announcement by a body of the CSA, and may be issued by any body of the CSA. A Notice shall be used for:

items.label: (a)
items.text: appointments, removals and changes of office;

items.label: (b)
items.text: decisions on individual matters;

items.label: (c)
items.text: instructions to the staff and bodies under the issuing body;

items.label: (d)
items.text: corrections under point 35 of this Order; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: announcements to the public.

items.after: A Notice shall not create, amend or repeal any rule, and shall not create any other document.

items.text: Documents published in the CSA Gazette rank in the following order, from highest to lowest: Acts, Director's Orders, Regulations, Guidelines and Notices. A document shall not be contrary to a document of a higher rank. Where a provision of a document is contrary to a document of a higher rank, that provision shall have no effect to the extent that it is contrary.
An enabling provision is a provision of a document that permits a body to create another document. Every enabling provision shall state:

items.label: (a)
items.text: the type of document that may be created;

items.label: (b)
items.text: the body that may create it; and

items.label: (c)
items.text: the matters that it may cover.
Documents may create other documents only as follows:

items.label: (a)
items.text: an Act may create Regulations and Guidelines;

items.label: (b)
items.text: a Director's Order may create Regulations and Guidelines;

items.label: (c)
items.text: a Regulation may create Guidelines;

items.label: (d)
items.text: a Guideline shall not create any other document, but may contain Appendices;

items.label: (e)
items.text: a Notice shall not create any other document; and

items.label: (f)
items.text: no document shall create an Act or a Director's Order.
A document created under an enabling provision:

items.label: (a)
items.text: shall state that enabling provision in (a) of its Article 1, in the form "This Regulation is made under Article 12 (a) of Act Number 2/2026 (Public Bonds Companies Act).";

items.label: (b)
items.text: shall not go beyond the matters stated in that enabling provision; and

items.label: (c)
items.text: shall not be contrary to the document that contains that enabling provision.

items.after: Only the body named in an enabling provision may create a document under it, and that body shall not transfer that power to another body unless the enabling provision permits it.

items.text: A body of the CSA may be established only by an Act or a Director's Order. A Regulation, Guideline or Notice shall not establish a body.
Every document shall be numbered strictly in the following forms, and no other number, prefix, suffix, volume or gazette identifier shall be added to a document number:

items.label: (a)
items.text: an Act: "Act Number #/year";

items.label: (b)
items.text: a Director's Order: "Director's Order Number #/year";

items.label: (c)
items.text: a Regulation: "R-#/year", cited as "Regulation Number R-#/year";

items.label: (d)
items.text: a Guideline: "G-#/year", cited as "Guideline Number G-#/year"; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: a Notice: the reference number of the issuing body.

items.after: In this point, "#" is the serial number of the document and "year" is the year in which the document is published, written in four digits. The number of a document shall be the same in every language in which the document is published.

items.text: The serial numbers of Acts, Director's Orders, Regulations and Guidelines shall be assigned by the Gazette Office. Each of these types shall have a single series of serial numbers for the whole CSA, which shall begin at 1 at the start of each year and continue in the order in which documents are accepted for publication. A number assigned to a document shall not be assigned to any other document, including after that document has been repealed. The reference number of a Notice shall be assigned by the issuing body, and shall not be used by that body for any other document.

An amendment shall be numbered as a new document in the series of the type of the document it amends. An amendment shall be titled by its order and by the number and title of the document it amends, in the form "First Amendment to Act Number 2/2026 (Public Bonds Companies Act)". The amendments to a document shall be counted in order: First, Second, Third, and so on.

Acts, Regulations and Guidelines shall be divided into Articles, which may be grouped into Chapters. Chapters and Articles shall be numbered in order, and Articles shall be numbered throughout the whole document without restarting in each Chapter. The points of an Article shall be numbered (a), (b), (c), and so on, and the points under them (1), (2), (3), and so on. These documents shall not use the words "section" or "subsection".

A Director's Order shall be written in numbered points, and the points under them shall be numbered (a), (b), (c), and so on. The reasons stated before the Director's decision shall be numbered separately, and are not points of the Order.
The schedules of a document shall be called Appendices, and shall be numbered in order: Appendix 1, Appendix 2, and so on.
Within the same document:

items.label: (a)
items.text: a point of the same Article shall be cited in the form "(a)(1) of this Article", where "this Article" refers to the whole Article;

items.label: (b)
items.text: another Article shall be cited in the form "Article 5 (a)(1) of this Act", using the words "this Act", "this Regulation", "this Guideline" or "this Policy", according to the type and title of the document;

items.label: (c)
items.text: a range of Articles shall be cited in the form "Articles 28 to 40 of this Act";

items.label: (d)
items.text: in a Director's Order, a point shall be cited in the form "point 5 (a) of this Order", and a point under the same point in the form "(a) of this point"; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: an Appendix shall be cited in the form "Appendix 2 of this Regulation".
Another document shall be cited in full each time it is cited, by its type, its number and its title in brackets, in the following forms:

items.label: (a)
items.text: an Act: "Article 23 (a)(1) of Act Number 1/2026 (title of the Act)";

items.label: (b)
items.text: a Director's Order: "point 4 (a) of Director's Order Number 1/2026 (title of the Order)";

items.label: (c)
items.text: a Regulation: "Article 5 (b) of Regulation Number R-3/2026 (title of the Regulation)";

items.label: (d)
items.text: a Guideline, including one titled a Policy: "Article 2 of Guideline Number G-1/2026 (title of the Guideline)"; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: a Notice: by its reference number, the name of the issuing body and the date of the Notice.

items.after: A document shall not cite the CSA Gazette, or any publication of the CSA Gazette, within its own text.

items.text: An Appendix shall not refer to the document it belongs to as "this Act", "this Order", "this Regulation", "this Guideline" or "this Policy". An Appendix shall cite the document it belongs to by the name of the issuing body and the type, number and title of the document, in the form "Article 23 of [issuing body]'s Act Number 2/2026 (Public Bonds Companies Act)".
Acts, Director's Orders, Regulations and Guidelines, and amendments to any of them, shall be published with a cover page. A cover page shall contain only:

items.label: (a)
items.text: the words "CSA Gazette";

items.label: (b)
items.text: the emblem and name of the issuing body;

items.label: (c)
items.text: the type and number of the document;

items.label: (d)
items.text: the title of the document; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: the date of publication.

items.after: A Notice shall not be published with a cover page. A Notice shall begin with the letterhead of the issuing body, with the reference number and date of the Notice directly below it, and shall end with the name, position and signature of the person who issues it and the stamp of the issuing body.

items.text: Every Act, Regulation and Guideline shall:

items.label: (a)
items.text: begin with an Article titled "Introduction and title", stating any enabling provision under which it is made and the title by which it shall be cited;

items.label: (b)
items.text: set out its purpose in its second Article;

items.label: (c)
items.text: state when it comes into force in its second last Article, and may set out the meaning of the words used in it in its last Article; and

items.label: (d)
items.text: end with the name, position and signature of the person who issues it on behalf of the issuing body, the date on which it is signed, and the stamp of the issuing body.
Every Director's Order shall be set out in the following order:

items.label: (a)
items.text: the number and title of the Order, followed by the words "Director's Order";

items.label: (b)
items.text: a statement by the Director, in the first person, introducing the Order;

items.label: (c)
items.text: the reasons for the Order, numbered in accordance with point 21 of this Order;

items.label: (d)
items.text: the authority under which the Order is issued;

items.label: (e)
items.text: the decision of the Director, in the first person;

items.label: (f)
items.text: the points of the Order;

items.label: (g)
items.text: a statement of the date and place at which the Order is issued; and

items.label: (h)
items.text: the signature, name and title of the Director, and the stamp of The Director's Office.

An Appendix may be prepared as a separate document and joined to the document it belongs to before publication. An Appendix forms part of that document and has the same effect as that document. Every Appendix shall be identifiable as part of its document if separated from it, and for this purpose shall:

items.label: (a)
items.text: begin with the letterhead of the issuing body, without a seal;

items.label: (b)
items.text: carry the Appendix number in a header on its first page only;

items.label: (c)
items.text: carry, on every page after the first, a header citing the number of the document and the provision under which the Appendix is made;

items.label: (d)
items.text: begin with an opening line citing the provision that refers to it, in the form "the [subject] stated in Article # (x) of [issuing body]'s Regulation Number R-#/year"; and

items.label: (e)
items.text: end with the stamp of the issuing body.

A document may be published in English, in Dhivehi, or in both languages. Where a document is published in both languages, the English and Dhivehi texts shall not differ, and shall carry the same meaning, the same provisions and the same numbering. The Gazette Office shall not publish a document in both languages unless the two texts carry the same meaning. In the Dhivehi text of a document, the types of documents shall be named as stated in point 6 of this Order, and document numbers shall be written in the same form as in the English text.

A document shall be submitted for publication by the issuing body to the Gazette Office at publish@gazette.csa, in its final form, signed and stamped, together with all its Appendices. A document to be published in both languages shall be submitted in both languages at the same time.
The Gazette Office shall review every document submitted to it for compliance with this Order before publication, and:

items.label: (a)
items.text: where the document does not comply with this Order, shall return it to the issuing body, stating each matter that does not comply; and

items.label: (b)
items.text: where the document complies with this Order, shall assign its number in accordance with point 18 of this Order and publish it on www.gazette.csa.

items.after: The Gazette Office shall not change the content of a document submitted to it. The date of publication of a document is the date on which it is published on www.gazette.csa.

items.text: A document shall come into force on the date of its publication, unless the document states a later date. A document shall not have effect before the date of its publication, unless the document expressly states otherwise.

The Gazette Office shall maintain a Gazette Register of every document published in the CSA Gazette, which shall be available to the public on www.gazette.csa. The Gazette Register shall record, for every document, its type, number, title, issuing body, date of publication, date of commencement and status. The status of a document shall be recorded as:

items.label: (a)
items.text: "In Force", where the document is in effect and has not been amended;

items.label: (b)
items.text: "Amended", where the document is in effect and has been amended; or

items.label: (c)
items.text: "Repealed", where the document has been repealed or has ceased to have effect.

A clerical or typographical error in a published document, and a difference between the English and Dhivehi texts of a document, shall be corrected by a Notice issued by the issuing body. The Notice shall state the document, the provision and the text being corrected, together with the corrected text. A correction shall not change the intended meaning or effect of a document. A change to the meaning or effect of a document shall be made only by an amendment under point 36 of this Order.

Except as stated in this point, a document shall be amended or repealed only by a document of the same type, issued by the body that issued the document being amended or repealed. An Act shall be amended or repealed in the same manner in which an Act is issued under point 7 of this Order at the time of the amendment or repeal. An amendment shall state each provision and Appendix that is added, changed or removed, and a document that has been amended shall be read together with all its amendments. A Notice shall not be amended, and may be withdrawn or replaced only by a new Notice of the issuing body.

A document shall cease to have effect on the date on which its repeal comes into force. Where a document is repealed, every document created under its enabling provisions shall cease to have effect on the same date, unless the repealing document states that it shall remain in force. A document that remains in force under this point shall continue to have effect until it is repealed.
This Order shall come into force on the date of its publication in the CSA Gazette.

blocks.text: This Order was issued on 07 November 2026 at The Director's Office, Washington, D.C.
